children: U.S. equities closed in the red but pared some losses after being deep in the negative on Thursday as discussions around the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz resurfaced.
The blue-chip Dow
closed -0.3%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) ended flat, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
finished even.
Washington and Tehran are exploring a
arrangement to restore commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz.
On a sector-by-sector stance, four of the 11 segments closed higher, with communication services leading the charge. At the other end of the spectrum, utilities suffered the most.

"Another day that was, indirectly, entirely about the Iran War. We’re at a breaking point, and the market knows it. The longer the conflict takes, the higher the inflation risks, as global energy supplies are at multi-year lows,” Seeking Alpha analyst Leo Nelissen of
said.
U.S. initial jobless claims for the week ended September 19 decreased by 1K to 197K from 198K in the previous week (revised from 196K), according to data released by the Department of Labor.
Furthermore, August U.S. New Home Sales rose +6.4% M/M to 684K compared to the 615K consensus figure.
The U.S. 2-year Treasury yield
climbed 2 basis points to 4.91%, the U.S. 10-year Treasury yield
moved up by 8 basis points to 5.19%, and the U.S. 30-year Treasury yield
pushed up 7 basis points to 5.47%.

“While there is still some more September to get through, stocks are so far bucking the historical trend of negative performance in September, suggesting that the earnings story that has been driving stocks may be more powerful than previously expected,” Glen Smith of GDS Wealth Management stated.
